title: Worst-case polylogarithmic fully dynamic planarity testing
formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic planarity structure with polylogarithmic worst-case edge-update time and constant-time planarity queries?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with words of Θ(log(n+2)) bits, unit-cost word arithmetic, Boolean operations, shifts, comparisons and memory accesses, and no nonuniform advice. Constants may be enlarged to address the stated space. The vertex set [n] is fixed, graphs are simple and undirected, and updates insert an absent edge or delete a present edge. Unless stated otherwise the graph starts empty; all outputs must be correct for every legal update sequence. Intermediate graphs may be nonplanar. A graph is planar when its vertices and edges can be drawn in the plane so that edges meet only at common endpoints. After every update a query must return the exact Boolean planarity value; neither an embedding nor an obstruction is requested. Require initialization O(n log^c(n+2)), space O((n+m)log^c(n+2)) words for current edge count m, O(log^c(n+2)) time for every individual update, and O(1) time for every query, for one absolute c. Rejected insertions or a promise that the graph stays planar are not allowed. The structure must reclaim unused edge storage within the stated space bound.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of the specified correctness and resource guarantees, or prove that this precise target is impossible. Any conditional impossibility must explicitly state its hypothesis and the implication proved.
context: Holm and Rotenberg already maintain the Boolean answer for arbitrary intermediate graphs in polylogarithmic amortized time. The remaining target strengthens that time guarantee.
why: This asks whether dynamic topological feasibility can avoid all occasional expensive updates.
